> [!TLDR]
> Inside the Kerr static limit, every physical observer must rotate; the region outside the horizon is the ergosphere.

<!-- Source: PDF page 204, printed page 188. -->

We now consider static observers in the Kerr spacetime. Such observers have a four-velocity proportional to the Killing vector $t^\alpha$:

$$
\mechanical{u^\alpha}=\mechanical{\gamma}t^\alpha, \tag{5.49}
$$

where the factor $\mechanical{\gamma}\equiv(-g_{\alpha\beta}t^\alpha t^\beta)^{-1/2}$ ensures that the four-velocity is properly normalized. Because these observers must be held in place by an external agent (a rocket engine, for example), the motion is not geodesic.

Static observers cannot exist everywhere in the Kerr spacetime. This can be seen from the fact that $t^\alpha$ is not everywhere timelike, but becomes null when $\mechanical{\gamma}^{-2}=-g_{tt}=0$; when this occurs, Eq. (5.49) breaks down. The *static limit* is

**Fig. 5.12** Static limit and event horizon of the Kerr spacetime.

therefore described by $g_{tt}=0$ or, after using Eqs. (5.44) and (5.45), $\mechanical{r}^2-2\mechanical{M}\mechanical{r}+\mechanical{a}^2\cos^2\mechanical{\theta}=0$. Solving for $\mechanical{r}$ reveals that the static limit is located at $\mechanical{r}=\mechanical{r_{\mathrm{sl}}}(\mechanical{\theta})$, where

$$
\mechanical{r_{\mathrm{sl}}}(\mechanical{\theta})=\mechanical{M}+\sqrt{\mechanical{M}^2-\mechanical{a}^2\cos^2\mechanical{\theta}}. \tag{5.50}
$$

Thus, observers cannot remain static when $\mechanical{r}\le\mechanical{r_{\mathrm{sl}}}(\mechanical{\theta})$, even if an arbitrarily large force is applied. Instead, the dragging of inertial frames compels them to rotate with the black hole. As we shall see, the static limit does not coincide with the hole’s event horizon. The finite region between the horizon and the static limit is called the *ergosphere* of the Kerr spacetime (Fig. 5.12).

## Physical quantities

| Symbol | Unit | Quantity | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\mechanical{u^\alpha}$ | — | Four-velocity | The static observer’s coordinate velocity components. |
| $\mechanical{\gamma}$ | $1$ | Time normalization factor | The factor that normalizes the static observer’s four-velocity. |
| $\mechanical{M}$ | $\unit{\mathrm m}$ | Black-hole mass | The mass in geometrized units. |
| $\mechanical{a}$ | $\unit{\mathrm m}$ | Specific angular momentum | The angular momentum divided by mass. |
| $\mechanical{r},\mechanical{r_{\mathrm{sl}}}$ | $\unit{\mathrm m}$ | Radius and static-limit radius | The radial coordinate and the limit of static observers. |
| $\mechanical{\theta}$ | $\unit{\mathrm{rad}}$ | Polar angle | The angle measured from the rotation axis. |
